recommendation: Keep the fix as-is. It is a narrow clarification in an active datatype narrative page, preserves the related SHALL NOT decision from FHIR-39176, and removes the residual ambiguity identified by FHIR-38957.
issue_request: FHIR-38957 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked to replace confusing prose about constraints on CodeableReference, CodeableReference.reference, and CodeableReference.concept with wording that specifically maps targetProfile constraints to reference and binding constraints to concept and prohibits specifying those constraints directly on the child elements.
initial_application: The CodeableReference paragraph was introduced by d621ab0bda, then edited by related FHIR-39132 and FHIR-39176 commits. Commit 0198f026142817d1711ee92eac43c72f246b77b9 explicitly applied FHIR-38957, but the current source still said the constraints apply to CodeableReference.reference or CodeableReference.concept 'respectively as appropriate', leaving residual ambiguity compared with the approved wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively maps codeablereference to the references page, making source/references.html current build input. StructureDefinition constraints sdf-24 and sdf-25 require targetProfile and binding constraints to be listed on the CodeableReference rather than on CodeableReference.reference or CodeableReference.concept. FHIR-39176 supports retaining SHALL NOT, and FHIR-I minutes confirm the FHIR-38957 Persuasive with Modification vote.
reconciliation: Updated source/references.html to say that targetProfile and binding constraints declared on CodeableReference apply to CodeableReference.reference and CodeableReference.concept respectively, and that these constraints SHALL NOT be specified directly on .reference or .concept.
source_changes: source/references.html: clarified the CodeableReference constraint sentence to use the approved one-to-one targetProfile/reference and binding/concept mapping.
